rationale: Round-4 duty, question 1: is the hook contract now fully anchored — can the WorktreeMain empty-Phase arm no longer produce nil post-initialization? Answer: NOT fully. 7cc6421a correctly closes the DERIVATION-FAILURE door (DerivationFailed -> ModeIndeterminate sentinel, nil narrowed, both new tests real and driving production wiring including the end-to-end Run('pre-commit', ..., ReadState, true) Block assertion — all verified), but one post-initialization empty-Phase door remains open, and I reproduced it EMPIRICALLY in a /tmp probe clone at exactly 7cc6421a (deleted after use): the WorktreeMain switch in derive.go has NO case for `err == nil && len(specs) > 1` — the multi-active-spec ambiguity arm (the trailing '// Multiple specs: leave specID empty (caller handles ambiguity)' comment) leaves Phase "" with DerivationFailed FALSE. ReadState's new sentinel branch keys ONLY on ctx.DerivationFailed, so this arm takes the else path, hs.Mode = "", and with no session file the narrowed nil check (`hs.Mode == "" && hs.SessionStartedAt == "" && !derivationFailed`) still fires: probe fixture with .beads/ present, bd healthy, TWO active spec epics -> ReadState() == nil -> runPreCommit's `st == nil` arm reads a genuinely-initialized, merely-ambiguous workspace as 'mindspec not initialized, allow' and PASSES a protected-branch commit. Three qualifications for the tally: (a) the runtime OUTCOME is pre-existing — pre-bead-5 this arm also produced "" -> nil -> allow, so this is not a bead-introduced regression; (b) the window is narrow (multiple active specs AND no .mindspec session.json AND a protected-branch commit); (c) BUT the round-4 commit's own comments assert invariants that are now demonstrably false — 'Only WorktreeMain's error arm reaches here with an otherwise-empty ctx.Phase' (the ambiguity arm reaches it with no error at all) and ''no state' is reachable ONLY via the two genuinely-pre-initialization checks above — never here' (my probe reached it post-initialization) — and the round-3 G1 principle being confirmed ('once .beads/ exists, X must never read as no state') is therefore only partially discharged. This is also a live contract DIVERGENCE inside the same bead: instruct_tail.go:30 treats `ctx.Phase == ""` as the ambiguity half of indeterminate (its comment names multi-active-spec as 'the only non-error way Phase stays ""'), while ReadState treats the identical Context as not-initialized nil. Same derived state, two contradictory honesty answers, both authored by bead 5. The fix is one predicate in the file this round already touched: mirror instruct_tail's exact condition (`ctx.DerivationFailed || ctx.Phase == ""` -> ModeIndeterminate) — safe because the two pre-initialization shapes can no longer reach this code (FindLocalRoot failure and BeadsDirMissing both return nil earlier, and WorktreeSpec/WorktreeBead Phases are always non-empty since round 1), so every remaining empty-Phase Context IS post-initialization ambiguity; blocking is also the designed-safe direction on a protected branch ('ANY mode'). Plus a multi-active-spec ReadState test (my probe fixture shape: two epics with spec_num/spec_title metadata via SetListJSONForTest) and corrected comments. Question 2: does any consumer of HookState.Mode mishandle the ModeIndeterminate sentinel? No. The complete consumer set is runPreCommit alone (hook.Run dispatches only 'pre-commit'; every other name returns Pass before touching stateFn). Traced ModeIndeterminate through each branch: protected branch -> Block fires in any mode and the message renders the honest 'mode: indeterminate' (the `if mode == "" { mode = "idle" }` cosmetic default no longer engages for a failure); non-protected spec/ branch -> indeterminate is neither ""/idle (early Pass) nor 'implement' (the only mode-gated Block), so Pass — identical outcome to every prior round and to pre-bead-5, fail-open on a non-protected branch being the hook's designed never-block posture, not a mishandling; no code path validates Mode against ValidModes (from which the sentinel is deliberately excluded), so nothing rejects or misroutes it. The sentinel choice itself is contract-sound: state.ModeIndeterminate already exists as the never-persisted rendering sentinel and ReadState is read-only, so no persistence surface can ingest it. Tests at this commit: internal/hook passes including both new round-4 tests; worktree left byte-identical; probe clone deleted.
concrete_changes_required: internal/hook/hook.go ReadState: extend the round-4 sentinel branch to the ambiguity half of the indeterminate contract — `if ctx.DerivationFailed || ctx.Phase == ""` -> `hs.Mode = state.ModeIndeterminate` (set the same `derivationFailed`-style non-nil latch) — mirroring cmd/mindspec/instruct_tail.go:30's exact predicate, so the WorktreeMain multi-active-spec arm (derive.go's uncovered `err == nil && len(specs) > 1` case, Phase "" with DerivationFailed false) can no longer reach the nil return post-initialization. Empirically reproduced at 7cc6421a: .beads/ present, bd healthy, two active spec epics -> ReadState() == nil -> runPreCommit allows a protected-branch commit as 'not initialized'. Safe: both genuine pre-initialization shapes already return nil BEFORE this code (FindLocalRoot failure; the round-2 BeadsDirMissing check), and WorktreeSpec/WorktreeBead never produce an empty Phase since round 1, so every empty-Phase Context reaching this line is post-initialization ambiguity. Correct the two now-false comments ('Only WorktreeMain's error arm...' and 'never here') in the same edit, and add the multi-active-spec ReadState unit pin (two epics with spec_num/spec_title metadata via phase.SetListJSONForTest -> non-nil, Mode == state.ModeIndeterminate). Note for the tally: the runtime outcome is PRE-EXISTING (pre-bead-5 identical), so if the tally rules it out-of-scope residual instead, the minimum in-bead ask is correcting the false invariant comments 7cc6421a itself introduced — but the one-predicate fix is smaller than this paragraph and completes round-3 G1's own stated principle.
